ciInvestigation.questionAsked: Do the two 20 s timeouts (txgioAddressResolve.integration.test.ts 'returns null for a genuinely nonexistent address'; txgioParcelStore.integration.test.ts 'issues exactly ONE extra statement per response for the join (no N+1)') come from re-enabling the atom-chain credential fallback in fetchPropertyAtomChain.ts, which could add a network call on those paths? Asked explicitly before these may be called CI noise.
ciInvestigation.answer: NO — established five ways, one of which is a controlled experiment on the identical commit.

evidence.method: Import-graph walk from disk (_scratch/p366-importgraph.mjs, no bundler).
evidence.result: lib/txgioAddressResolve.ts has a 16-file import closure and lib/txgioParcelStore.ts a 5-file closure; NEITHER closure contains any lib/buildableEnvelope/* file. The two timing-out files cannot reach the changed code by import at all — so no code path of theirs was altered. (canva-route.test.ts DOES reach it, but only through the routes barrel: canva-route.test.ts -> __tests__/setup.ts -> routes/index.ts -> routes/brokerageBrief.ts -> routes/brokeragePlaceBuildableEnvelope.ts. That is a module-level import which never calls resolveSpineZoningWhenGisAbsent, and the parcel-record read this lane adds is a dynamic import() INSIDE that function.)

evidence.method: Can the re-enabled fallback fetch at all in CI?
evidence.result: .github/workflows/pr-checks.yml contains ZERO `secrets.` references. RETRIEVAL_API_KEY, HAUSKA_RETRIEVAL_API_KEY and BRIEF_RETRIEVAL_API_KEY appear ONLY in cloud-run-deploy.yml (production). src/__tests__/setup.ts sets no retrieval name. With no key mounted, fetchPropertyAtomChain and districtFromAtomChain both hit `if (!key) return null` BEFORE any fetch — the fallback is inert in every test job, so it cannot add a network call there regardless of which test runs.

evidence.method: CONTROLLED EXPERIMENT — re-run the identical commit (the decisive one).
evidence.result: Commit 773879ec was re-run as run 35413841352 attempt 2. ATTEMPT 1: Test FAILED with canva-route + txgioAddressResolve + txgioParcelStore. ATTEMPT 2: Test PASSED. Same commit, same tests, opposite outcome. The only job still red on attempt 2 is Typecheck, and only because 773879ec still carries the TS2352 this lane then fixed in ecaf5bfc. A failure that disappears when unchanged code is re-run is not caused by that code.

vitest.config.ts runs fileParallelism: true with singleFork: false (its own comment: 'Each file gets its own worker so per-file PG schemas + test-context state never leak across files') — every one of ~408 test files is a parallel forked worker hitting ONE Postgres service container — with testTimeout: 20_000, exactly the number both failures report. Both failing cases are the heaviest in their files (withTestSchema + situs resolution; the N+1 statement-count case) in files where every case already takes 2-8 s. This is connection contention, not a code path.

Across the last 25 PR Checks runs the Test job failed 2 times (8%). The two failure sets are DISJOINT: this lane failed canva-route / txgioAddressResolve / txgioParcelStore; the sibling p340 lane failed queue.test.ts and reasoningAtoms.test.ts. Failures that migrate between runs and share no tests are load-sensitive, not a deterministic regression.

missionPremise: OPS-24 law and the 2026-09-11 serving-path decision (_decisions/2026-09-11_ledger_as_serving_path_seven_steps.md, ADR-031 amendment, OPS-23 section 0): the ledger is the serving path, atoms are canonical, and every surface consumes one gated reader. The lane's premise is that when a drawing route and a card disagree about a parcel's district, the route is reading an older or narrower source than the ledger the card serves.

leave_behind: THE FLEET GATE DEFECT (new, and the most valuable thing this lane found): the api-server Test job flakes at ~8% (2 of the last 25 PR Checks runs) because vitest.config.ts runs fileParallelism: true with singleFork: false — ~408 parallel forked workers against ONE Postgres service container — under testTimeout: 20_000. The failing tests MIGRATE between runs and share nothing (this lane: canva-route/txgioAddressResolve/txgioParcelStore; p340: queue/reasoningAtoms). Concrete remedy for whoever owns that gate: raise testTimeout for the DB-heavy integration files, or bound concurrency for files that create their own schemas. Deliberately NOT applied here — bumping a timeout inside a zoning-read PR would mask a fleet issue and edit a gate this lane does not own.

The CI evidence for PR #726 could NOT be produced locally and must be read from CI: the checkout at P:/legacy-design-tools is 524 commits behind origin/main and its node_modules predates @empressaio/setback-corpus, so 12 api-server suites fail to LOAD there ('Cannot find package @empressaio/setback-corpus/resolve'). The local Postgres on 5432 also lacks the vector and postgis extensions the DB integration tests require, so even the two timing-out files could not be reproduced faithfully on this machine. Both limitations are named rather than worked around.
